tagline.text: The heart of the Philippines, where Moriones masks walk the streets

image.credit: Benedict Esber / CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons

items.credit: Emman A. Foronda / CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons

children.text: A heart-shaped island at the geographic center of the Philippine archipelago, earning it the nickname "the heart of the Philippines." Every Holy Week, Moriones parade through the streets in Roman soldier masks, while the 1792 fortress church of Boac Cathedral, the white sand of Maniwaya Island, and the Tres Reyes Islands round out a quiet island getaway.

Marinduque is a round island floating between Tayabas Bay and the Sibuyan Sea south of Luzon. Seen on a map it resembles a heart, and because it sits almost at the very center of the Philippine archipelago, it has earned the nickname "the heart of the Philippines." Six towns — Boac, Mogpog, Gasan, Buenavista, Torrijos, and Santa Cruz — ring the island, and around the capital Boac, Spanish-era lanes and wooden houses remain relatively well preserved.

What made the island famous nationwide is Moriones, held during Holy Week. Wearing Roman soldier helmets and masks, residents fill the streets for a full week, re-enacting the story of Longinus, the soldier who pierced Jesus's side with a spear and was healed and converted. It is said to have begun in the early 1800s with a parish priest in Mogpog, and residents still hand-carve the masks from wood today, wearing them for several years in fulfillment of a religious vow.

The cathedral on the hill in Boac is the island's history made stone. During the 18th century, when Moro pirate raids were frequent, residents built a tall stone wall around the church to use as a refuge, and the current building was completed in 1792. Legend holds that the church's enshrined image, Our Lady of Biglang-Awa (Our Lady of Sudden Mercy), drove off the pirates, and the cathedral is designated a National Cultural Treasure.

There are no big resorts or busy commercial strips, but within a day or two you can reach a wide range of scenery: Maniwaya and Mongpong Islands off Santa Cruz, the Tres Reyes Islands off Gasan, the Malbog sulfur hot spring in Buenavista, and Mount Malindig, the island's highest peak. It suits travelers who want to witness a traditional Filipino Catholic festival up close, or anyone looking for a quiet island not too far from Manila.

During Holy Week, processions of Roman soldier masks fill the streets of Boac, Mogpog, and Gasan. The festival peaks on Easter with the "Pugutan," a re-enactment of Longinus being chased down, captured, and executed.

children.text: Below the cathedral, the Mataas na Bayan area is lined with two-story wooden houses from the Spanish and American eras. The provincial museum displays Moriones masks and the island's history.
A white sand island off Santa Cruz; Palad Sandbar, which emerges in the middle of the sea at low tide, is about
10–20 minutes
away by boat.
Three islands off Gasan — Gaspar, Melchor, and Baltazar — named after the Three Wise Men. The waters around Gaspar Island are known as a snorkeling and diving spot.
A hot spring rising at the foot of Mount Malindig in Buenavista, where you can soak in sulfur-scented warm water and ease the fatigue of island travel.
A dormant volcano
high, the tallest point on the island. The forest is dense, so climbers go with a local guide, and near the summit you can see the whole island and the Sibuyan Sea.

A giant Marian statue stands on the hill at the entrance to Balanacan Port in Mogpog, where boats arrive. It's a good spot to look down over boats entering the narrow cove and the fishing village scenery.

If you're visiting during Holy Week, it's better to adjust the itinerary to stay in Boac or Mogpog from Thursday through Easter Sunday, so you can watch the processions and the Longinus re-enactment.
This is the most common route. From Cubao, Buendia, or PITX in Manila, take a JAC Liner or DLTB bus to Lucena in Quezon province in about
3–5 hours
, for about
. From the Lucena Grand Terminal, take a jeepney or tricycle to Dalahican port, then a Starhorse Shipping or Montenegro Shipping roll-on/roll-off boat to Balanacan port in Mogpog, about
3–4 hours
across. The regular adult boat fare is about
, with sailings every 2–4 hours from early morning to night. The whole trip from Manila takes about
7–9 hours
There is also a direct route where the bus is loaded onto the ferry and continues from Cubao to Santa Cruz. Fares run about
to Mogpog and about
to Santa Cruz, with roughly one trip a day in the afternoon, so reserve ahead. With no transfers, it's convenient for travelers with a lot of luggage.
Marinduque Airport (MRQ) in Gasan exists, but scheduled commercial flights have stopped and restarted repeatedly, and no scheduled service is confirmed as of
. Small propeller planes have not been able to depart Manila's airport since
March 29, 2026
, so if service resumes, it will likely be from Clark. Check with the airline before departure whether flights are operating, and if not, use the bus and boat route. From the airport to Boac is about
15 minutes
by tricycle.
Jeepneys and vans to each town wait outside Balanacan Port, timed to boat arrivals. It's about
20–30 minutes
to Boac, for around
. The road around the island is about
120km
, which you can circle in a day by chartered tricycle or a van with a driver (about
per day). Maniwaya Island is about
20–30 minutes
away by bangka from Buyabod Port in Santa Cruz.
December–May
is the dry season and the best time for island hopping and driving.
March–May
especially brings calm seas and clear water, but midday temperatures can climb to
, so bring a hat and water. The Moriones Festival is held each year between
late March and April
, depending on the date of Easter, and boats and lodging get very crowded that week, so book several weeks ahead.
June–November

is the wet season, with frequent afternoon showers, and the Lucena–Balanacan boat is suspended when typhoons pass through southern Luzon. Even in the wet season you can still walk the heritage sites in Boac town, but island hopping and the Mount Malindig trek may be cancelled depending on the weather, so it's wise to keep a spare day.

For a heritage-focused trip, staying in Boac town is most convenient — small hotels and pensions run about

a night, and the cathedral, market, and jeepney stops are all within walking distance. To enjoy the sea, beach resorts along the Gasan and Torrijos coasts, or cottage-style lodging and campsites on Maniwaya Island, are good choices. Lodging on Maniwaya Island runs about
a night, though some places only have electricity in the evening. Rooms fill up early during Holy Week, so looking into a homestay is another option.

Marinduque's signature snack is uraro (arrowroot) cookies, soft treats baked from the flour of a root crop similar to kudzu, melting in your mouth and popular as souvenirs. Chewy kalamay, made from rice, coconut milk, and brown sugar, is also well known. Restaurants commonly serve ginataan (fish and vegetables simmered in coconut milk), freshly grilled seafood, and tangy sinigang soup. A meal at a local carinderia costs about
, and during Moriones, snack stalls line the streets.
Boat tickets can be bought at the Dalahican Port counter or booked online. Tickets sell out during Holy Week and long weekends, so reserve online in advance.
From
March 2026

, boarding a Montenegro Shipping boat at Lucena port requires registering in advance in the Online Reservation Assistance System (ORAS), under Philippine Ports Authority (PPA) guidelines. You can register through the QR code on the port notice; passengers who have already bought tickets online and passengers traveling with a vehicle are exempt.

Moriones isn't a single parade in one place — it runs all week across several towns. Check each town's tourism office for the schedule of the Good Friday procession and the Easter Longinus re-enactment.
Shops and restaurants close on Holy Thursday and Good Friday, and transport also becomes limited. Stock up on water and snacks beforehand.
ATMs are only found in larger towns like Boac and Santa Cruz, so bring cash for island hopping costs.
Palad Sandbar only appears at low tide, so check the tide schedule before island hopping and coordinate your departure time with the boatman.
Mount Malindig's forest is dense with few trail markers, so you must hire a local guide through the registration desk on the Buenavista side.
Avoid sightseeing in the cathedral during Mass, and it's polite to avoid shorts or sleeveless tops.

During Holy Week, the Lucena–Balanacan boat gets packed with travelers heading home, and it's common to be unable to get a ticket or to wait for hours. Book your round-trip boat tickets in advance, and check the latest notices for the festival schedule and boat timetable.
Moriones participants are devotees fulfilling a religious vow. Don't force off their masks or block the procession, and ask permission before taking close-up photos.
The Boac River area, contaminated by the 1996 Marcopper mining disaster, is still recovering, so it's best not to swim or fish in the river.
Island-hopping bangkas don't sail when waves are high. Wear a life jacket, and don't push to go out on bad-weather days.
After dark, the road around the island has few streetlights, making motorbike riding dangerous.
The hot spring water is hot and strongly sulfurous, so don't soak too long, and remove any precious metal jewelry beforehand.
